label: late original-phase input of o/q/e/l/g/3/v/b/m after a prefix containing y/digits/d/c/p/r/u/f
explanation: Fires almost only during the original (input) phase at positions t>=3, mostly t=4-8 (99.9% of mass). It never fires at t=0-2 or during the copy phase, and fires only trivially at <DEL>. The current input token is the main gate: o and q (about 5.7% rate each), then e, l, g, 3, v, b, m. It almost never fires on a, x or w, and the listed tokens cover about 98% of mass. Within those steps it fires much more when the earlier prefix holds several of y, digits 0-2, d, c, p, r, u, f; first_tok y or a digit has the highest lift. So it looks like a gradual integration of prefix composition, not a crisp rule. Requiring at least 2 such prefix tokens keeps about 93% of mass at roughly 23% precision on dev. Requiring at least 3 roughly doubles precision but drops recall to about 57%. Activations are stronger on first occurrences of the input token (in_first=1 holds 92% of mass). Precision is limited because most qualifying steps stay below threshold.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the current input token, by step (t=7: o, q, l, e; t=4: q, o, e, l; t=3: o, q, e, l) and the first original token (most: y, 1, 0, r, 2, d; least: l, q, o, e); timing cues that raise it most: t=5, t=4, t=6.
